notes: §1985:IX.4.8.2 prints USE AFTER STANDARD { EXCEPTION | ERROR } PROCEDURE ON { { file-name-1 } ... | INPUT | OUTPUT | I-O | EXTEND }, with USE, AFTER, EXCEPTION / ERROR and PROCEDURE underlined and STANDARD and ON not. The superset Format 1 alternative of useStatement (USE GLOBAL? AFTER? STANDARD? (EXCEPTION | ERROR) PROCEDURE? ON? useOnTarget) with useOnTarget (one open mode, or fileName+) parses it, and the 1985 edition reaches its two required words through VisitUseStatement, which at --std 85 refuses a Format 1 USE without AFTER (use-without-after-2002) and without PROCEDURE (use-without-procedure-2002), both COBOL0900; the same visitor refuses the 2002 formats USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION / EC and EXCEPTION OBJECT / EO. DeclBindUse binds the operand: one open mode per statement or the list of file-names. Probed at 85: USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON F1 F2 runs the procedure for each file's failed OPEN, USE AFTER ERROR PROCEDURE INPUT (STANDARD and ON omitted) and ... ON I-O run for the matching open mode only, ... ON EXTEND compiles; USE STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ..., USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR ON ..., ON INPUT OUTPUT, ON F1 INPUT, EXCEPTION ERROR together, ON with no operand, and USE AFTER EC EC-I-O are each refused. GLOBAL, which this format does not print, is the Inter-Program Communication module's addition to the same statement (§1985:X.5.5.2) and is rightly accepted at 85. The witness declares USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON one indexed file and shows the procedure run on a READ of an absent key.

next.reason: 1985: "USE AFTER STANDARD {EXCEPTION|ERROR} PROCEDURE ON ... (AFTER underlined, required; no GLOBAL)"; 2023: "USE [ GLOBAL ] AFTER STANDARD ... (AFTER printed without underlining, so optional; GLOBAL added)". Same file-exception alternatives, but 2023 adds an optional GLOBAL phrase and makes AFTER optional, so it accepts programs that the 1985 format refused.
